characters.name: Time Traveller
characters.description: A lean middle-aged Victorian inventor with pale gray eyes, short graying brown hair, a cream shirt, dark waistcoat and practical brown coat. Energetic and thoughtful.

characters.name: Narrator
characters.description: Unnamed first‑person observer. Middle‑aged gentleman in dark frock coat, watch chain, sober expression. Attentive, asks questions and keeps the Time Traveller's two white flowers.

characters.name: Weena
characters.description: A small adult Eloi woman with short soft fair curls, bright eyes and a simple lavender tunic with sandals. Gentle and trusting, carrying two small white flowers. Clearly an adult with a slight build.

characters.name: Eloi (group)
characters.description: Surface people: slight, graceful, childlike adults. Bareheaded, soft-skinned, clothed in light purple or white tunics, sandals, minimal ornament. Move in idle, melodic ways; often distracted.

characters.name: Morlocks (group)
characters.description: Subterranean workers: pale, hair-light, lithe and furtive. Large grey‑red reflective eyes, long fingers, ragged dark undergarments, adapted to gloom. Move with quick, crawling gait and hissed vocal noises.

characters.name: Medical Man
characters.description: The Doctor in the drawing-room. Sturdy, practical, black frock coat, medical pocket case. Skeptical but observant of injuries and evidence.

characters.name: Psychologist
characters.description: Thoughtful, spectacled guest. Slim, tidy coat, analytical expression. Prompted the model demonstration and debates Time Traveller’s ideas.

characters.name: Editor
characters.description: Portly, impatient man in a tweed waistcoat. Quick with a jeer or a newspaper quip; present at the dinner table and later.

characters.name: Filby
characters.description: Red‑haired, argumentative young man. Bright eyes, quick tongue, often interrupts with incredulous exclamations.

characters.name: Journalist
characters.description: Animated, notebook‑bearing man. Lively, forward; often laughs but listens for a good story.

source.name: The Time Machine by H. G. Wells (1895)

pages.title: A Machine That Vanishes
pages.text: At dinner, an inventor showed his friends a tiny machine. He said it could travel through time. When a lever moved, the little machine vanished! His guests were amazed, but some thought it was a trick. In his workshop stood a larger machine, big enough to carry a person.
pages.scene: A Victorian sitting room by a warm fire. The Time Traveller and his friend the Narrator lean over a small brass model on a low table as its edges shimmer and fade. A few guests watch in wonder. Warm lamplight, precise ink lines with blue and amber washes.

pages.title: Far Into the Future
pages.text: The inventor sat in the larger machine and moved its lever. Day and night flashed past. Buildings changed, and whole seasons seemed to flicker in moments. He stopped in the year 802,701. His workshop was gone. He had arrived in a strange garden beside a huge white statue.
pages.scene: The Time Traveller sits in a human-sized brass-and-ebony time machine with a padded seat and large circular frame. Blurred seasons and buildings sweep past outside his workshop window. His hands hold two small control levers. Wonder and movement, one coherent portrait scene, no readable numbers.

pages.title: A Beautiful World, a Missing Machine
pages.text: Small, gentle people called the Eloi welcomed him with flowers and fruit. Their world seemed peaceful. But when he returned to the garden, his machine had disappeared. Without it, he could never get home. Marks in the grass led toward the white statue, whose base had locked metal doors.
pages.scene: A lush future garden beside a large white winged sphinx on a bronze base. The Time Traveller kneels beside a flattened patch of grass where his machine stood. Several small adult Eloi in light tunics watch from a distance. Bright flowers contrast with his worried expression.

pages.title: A Friend Named Weena
pages.text: One day he saw an Eloi named Weena struggling in the river. He saved her, while the others did little to help. After that, Weena stayed close to him and gave him flowers. She was frightened of the dark. Her fear suggested that this lovely world was hiding something.
pages.scene: The Time Traveller and Weena sit safely on a sunny riverbank after her rescue. Weena, a small adult Eloi woman with short fair curls and a lavender tunic, offers him two white flowers. Calm water and distant ruins behind them. Focus on gratitude and friendship, not danger. The time machine is missing at this point in the story. No time machine, brass chair, circular frame or other vehicle is present.

pages.title: The People Underground
pages.text: Beneath the ground lived pale people called Morlocks. They worked among old machines and could see in the dark. The Traveller guessed that a deep divide between rich and poor had changed humanity over thousands of years. Now the Eloi lived above, while the Morlocks hunted them at night.
pages.scene: At the mouth of an underground shaft, the Time Traveller peers cautiously into a distant machinery hall. Two pale adult Morlocks with large reflective eyes stand far below among wheels and pipes. Small warm light in his hand contrasts with cool shadows. No hunting, attack or injuries.

pages.title: The Old Museum
pages.text: The Traveller and Weena walked to a great ruined building. It had once been a museum. He hoped to find tools that could help him open the statue’s doors and recover his machine. Among the dusty displays, he found matches and other useful supplies. They had stayed too long: night was coming.

He holds a small supply box while Weena looks toward the darkening windows. Grand scale, quiet discovery, no readable labels. The time machine is missing at this point in the story. pages.title: Lost in the Fire
pages.text: They tried to cross the woods in darkness. Morlocks followed them, and the Traveller used fire to keep them back. But the flames spread through the trees. In the fear and confusion, he lost Weena. He searched and called for her, but she was gone. He believed she had died.

pages.title: The Trap at the Statue
pages.text: The metal doors beneath the white statue were open. Inside waited his machine. The Morlocks had set a trap! The doors shut behind him, and the room went dark. He reached the seat, fitted the control levers and escaped through time. Once more, the world rushed past him.
pages.scene: Inside a bronze chamber beneath the sphinx, the Time Traveller reaches the seat of his full-sized brass time machine. A door is closing behind him, with indistinct Morlock silhouettes beyond it. Blue-white light begins to swirl around the machine. No physical attack or injury.

pages.title: The Far End of Time
pages.text: He travelled much farther into the future. The sun looked huge and red above a cold, silent shore. Strange creatures moved beside the sea, and the air was hard to breathe. At last, almost all life seemed gone. Frightened by this lonely future, he turned the machine toward home.
pages.scene: The Time Traveller sits beside his machine on a lonely far-future shore beneath an enormous dull red sun. Dark water meets a stony beach, with small unfamiliar crab-like creatures in the distance. Quiet awe and desolation, muted red and blue washes, no action or lettering.

pages.title: Back at the Dinner Table
pages.text: He returned to his own time, tired, hungry and shaken. His friends listened as he told them what had happened. Some doubted his story. Then he showed them the two strange white flowers Weena had given him. They were small reminders of kindness in a world so far away.
pages.scene: A Victorian dining room at night. The tired Time Traveller places two small white flowers on the table while the Narrator and a few dinner guests listen. His rumpled coat contrasts with the neat room. Warm lamplight, thoughtful faces, the flowers as the visual focus.

pages.title: One More Journey
pages.text: The next day, his friend came back to the workshop. The Traveller was preparing to leave again, this time with a camera and a bag. He promised to return soon. Then the machine flashed, blurred and vanished. His friend waited, hoping to hear another extraordinary story.
pages.scene: In the workshop, the Time Traveller sits in his machine with a simple camera and travel bag. The Narrator stands in the doorway as the machine begins to become transparent. Morning light through high windows, a sudden rush of air, no readable signs or diagrams.

pages.title: Two Flowers Remain
pages.text: Three years passed, and the Traveller still had not returned. His friend wondered where—and when—he might be. The future remained a mystery. But he kept Weena’s two flowers. Though they had dried and faded, they reminded him that kindness could survive even in a very different world.
pages.scene: The Narrator sits at a quiet writing desk in soft afternoon light, looking at two dried white flowers resting on a plain sheet of paper. An empty workshop doorway is visible behind him. Gentle, reflective ending, crisp ink details and restrained warm washes, no readable writing.
